areas.name: South Minneapolis
areas.lede: Lakes, creeks and parkways, and street after street of bungalows, foursquares, Tudors and period-revival homes from the early twentieth century.

neighborhoods.name: East Harriet
neighborhoods.line: Early-twentieth-century homes beside Lake Harriet and the Lyndale Park gardens.

neighborhoods.name: Kingfield
neighborhoods.line: Bungalows, foursquares and two-stories close to the shops of Nicollet Avenue.

neighborhoods.name: Lynnhurst
neighborhoods.line: Period-revival and Tudor homes between Lake Harriet and Minnehaha Creek.

neighborhoods.name: Tangletown
neighborhoods.line: Curving streets around the Washburn Water Tower, with Tudor and Arts and Crafts homes.

neighborhoods.name: Fulton
neighborhoods.line: Craftsman and period-revival homes west of Lake Harriet, near 50th & France.

neighborhoods.name: Linden Hills
neighborhoods.line: Craftsman homes and cottages between Lake Harriet and Bde Maka Ska, around a village of small shops.

neighborhoods.name: Armatage
neighborhoods.line: Postwar and mid-century homes in the southwest corner of the city.

neighborhoods.name: Around Lake Nokomis
neighborhoods.line: Bungalows and period homes near Lake Nokomis and Minnehaha Creek.

areas.name: Around the Lakes
areas.lede: The neighborhoods around Lake of the Isles, Bde Maka Ska and Cedar Lake, where many of the city's grandest early-1900s homes stand.

neighborhoods.name: Kenwood
neighborhoods.line: Early-twentieth-century homes on winding streets between Lake of the Isles and Cedar Lake.

neighborhoods.name: East Isles
neighborhoods.line: Early-1900s homes along the east shore of Lake of the Isles.

neighborhoods.name: Lowry Hill
neighborhoods.line: Grand early-1900s homes on the hill above the Walker Art Center and the Sculpture Garden.

neighborhoods.name: ECCO
neighborhoods.line: Early-twentieth-century homes between Bde Maka Ska and the shops of Uptown.

neighborhoods.name: CARAG
neighborhoods.line: Early-1900s homes on walkable blocks near Bde Maka Ska and Uptown.

neighborhoods.name: Bryn Mawr
neighborhoods.line: Craftsman and Tudor homes tucked beside Theodore Wirth Park.

areas.name: St. Paul
areas.lede: Victorian and early-twentieth-century homes south of I-94, from the mansions of Summit Avenue to the tree-lined blocks around Grand Avenue.

neighborhoods.name: Summit Hill
neighborhoods.line: Victorian and early-twentieth-century homes along Summit and Grand Avenues.

neighborhoods.name: Macalester-Groveland
neighborhoods.line: Early-twentieth-century homes around Macalester College and Grand Avenue.

neighborhoods.name: Crocus Hill
neighborhoods.line: Victorian and early-1900s homes on quiet streets just south of Summit Avenue.

neighborhoods.name: Ramsey Hill
neighborhoods.line: Some of St. Paul's most ornate Victorian homes, near the Cathedral and the east end of Summit Avenue.

neighborhoods.name: Highland Park
neighborhoods.line: Period-revival and mid-century homes near the Mississippi River bluffs.

areas.name: Edina
areas.lede: From the 1920s period-revival homes of the Country Club District to the city's postwar and mid-century neighborhoods.

neighborhoods.name: Country Club
neighborhoods.line: A planned 1920s neighborhood of period-revival homes near 50th & France.

neighborhoods.name: Morningside
neighborhoods.line: Cottage-scale 1920s to 1940s homes on the Minneapolis border.

neighborhoods.name: Parkwood Knolls
neighborhoods.line: Postwar and mid-century homes on wooded lots.

neighborhoods.name: Mid-century Edina
neighborhoods.line: Mid-century modern and postwar homes across the city's later neighborhoods.

areas.name: Golden Valley
areas.lede: Wooded hills and one of the Twin Cities' strongest collections of mid-century modern homes.

neighborhoods.name: Tyrol Hills
neighborhoods.line: Wooded hills and a notable collection of mid-century modern homes.

neighborhoods.name: Mid-century Golden Valley
neighborhoods.line: Mid-century modern and postwar homes across the city's wooded neighborhoods.
